1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Installs or builds the Callisto binary. Factored out of action.yml so
     3	# callisto-action's own environment setup can call it directly by path
     4	# (github.action_path has no ref-ambiguous `uses:` to resolve), instead of
     5	# duplicating this logic.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	
     8	# Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
     9	# tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
    10	# "git add -A").
    11	CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
    12	mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
    13	TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"
    14	SOURCE="$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    15	
    16	if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
    17	  echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
    18	  exit 1
    19	fi
    20	
    21	# With no explicit version override, install the release this action's own
    22	# invocation is pinned to (GITHUB_ACTION_REF, github.action_ref) rather than
    23	# whatever is newest, so `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` always
    24	# installs X.Y.Z. Falls back to true "latest" when the ref is unset (local or
    25	# unpinned invocation) or matches no published callisto@ tag.
    26	if [[ "$SOURCE" == "auto" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" && -n "${GITHUB_ACTION_REF:-}" ]]; then
    27	  resolved_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git 'callisto@*' 2>/dev/null \
    28	    | awk -v ref="$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" '$1 == ref { print $2 }' \
    29	    | sed -e 's#^refs/tags/##' -e 's/\^{}$//' \
    30	    | sort -V | tail -n1) || true
    31	  if [[ -n "$resolved_tag" ]]; then
    32	    echo "Resolved action ref $GITHUB_ACTION_REF to $resolved_tag"
    33	    TAG_NAME="$resolved_tag"
    34	  fi
    35	fi
    36	
    37	# Validate verification mode
    38	VERIFICATION="${INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION:-fallback}"
    39	case "$VERIFICATION" in
    40	  require|fallback|skip) ;;
    41	  *)
    42	    echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto verification '$VERIFICATION' (valid values: require, fallback, skip)"
    43	    exit 1
    44	    ;;
    45	esac
    46	
    47	# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
    48	OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    49	ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)
    50	
    51	if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
    52	  if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "arm64" ]]; then
    53	    ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
    54	  else
    55	    ASSET_NAME=""
    56	  fi
    57	elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == "linux" ]]; then
    58	  if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "x86_64" ]]; then
    59	    ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
    60	  else
    61	    ASSET_NAME=""
    62	  fi
    63	elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == *"mingw"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"msys"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"windows"* ]]; then
    64	  ASSET_NAME=""
    65	else
    66	  ASSET_NAME=""
    67	fi
    68	
    69	if [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]]; then
    70	  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/latest/download/$ASSET_NAME"
    71	elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]]; then
    72	  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/$TAG_NAME/$ASSET_NAME"
    73	fi
    74	
    75	# Derive a crates.io version spec from TAG_NAME: "latest" installs
    76	# whatever crates.io resolves as latest (no --version flag); an
    77	# explicit tag ("callisto@0.5.0" or legacy "callisto-cli@0.5.0")
    78	# strips either prefix down to the bare semver cargo install expects.
    79	CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto@}"; CRATE_VERSION="${CRATE_VERSION#callisto-cli@}"
    80	
    81	# Pick a download destination whose extension matches ASSET_NAME
    82	# (under $RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace) so the extraction step
    83	# below always has an archive it can actually open -- a hardcoded
    84	# ".tar.gz" path here previously masked the fact that Windows assets
    85	# are zip files, since tar -xzf can't read a zip regardless of what
    86	# the file on disk is really named.
    87	case "$ASSET_NAME" in
    88	  *.zip)
    89	    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.zip"
    90	    ;;
    91	  *.tar.gz)
    92	    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    93	    ;;
    94	  *)
    95	    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    96	    ;;
    97	esac
    98	
    99	# A prebuilt asset runs with the job's privileges, so it must carry a
   100	# GitHub attestation from the Callisto release workflow before it is
   101	# extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
   102	# returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.
   103	verify_asset() {
   104	  local reason=""
   105	  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "skip" ]]; then
   106	    echo "::warning::verification=skip: $ASSET_NAME was not verified"
   107	    return 0
   108	  fi
   109	  if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   110	    reason="gh is not installed"
   111	  elif ! gh attestation verify "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" \
   112	      --repo orin-dx/callisto \
   113	      --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
   114	      --deny-self-hosted-runners; then
   115	    reason="attestation verification failed"
   116	  fi
   117	  [[ -z "$reason" ]] && return 0
   118	  rm -f "$DOWNLOAD_DEST"
   119	  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "require" ]]; then
   120	    echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"
   121	    exit 1
   122	  fi
   123	  echo "::warning::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason; discarding it and installing from crates.io (verification=fallback)"
   124	  return 1
   125	}
   126	
   127	# Download, verify and extract the prebuilt asset; nonzero means use the fallback chain.
   128	fetch_prebuilt() {
   129	  curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" 2>/dev/null || return 1
   130	  verify_asset || return 1
   131	  # Extract only the expected binary, never the whole archive.
   132	  case "$ASSET_NAME" in
   133	    *.zip)
   134	      unzip -q "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" callisto.exe -d "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
   135	      ;;
   136	    *)
   137	      tar -xzf "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" -C "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" callisto
   138	      ;;
   139	  esac
   140	}
   141	
   142	# Dependencies named callisto-cli do not establish checkout source ownership.
   143	owns_local_source() {
   144	  local workspace git_root metadata
   145	  workspace=$(cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && pwd -P) || return 1
   146	  git_root=$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse --show-toplevel) || return 1
   147	  [[ "$git_root" == "$workspace" ]] || return 1
   148	  git -C "$workspace" ls-files --error-unmatch -- \
   149	    Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs >/dev/null || return 1
   150	  metadata=$(cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1 \
   151	    --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml") || return 1
   152	  jq -e --arg workspace "$workspace" '
   153	    .workspace_root == $workspace and
   154	    (.workspace_members as $members | [.packages[] |
   155	      select(.name == "callisto-cli" and .source == null and
   156	        .manifest_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml") and
   157	        (.id as $id | $members | index($id) != null) and
   158	        any(.targets[]; .name == "callisto" and (.kind | index("bin") != null) and
   159	          .src_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs")))] | length == 1)
   160	  ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null
   161	}
   162	
   163	if [[ "$SOURCE" == "local" ]]; then
   164	  if ! owns_local_source; then
   165	    echo "::error::setup-callisto source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout; check out Callisto source or use source=auto"
   166	    exit 1
   167	  fi
   168	  echo "Building local callisto binary from current repository commit..."
   169	  cargo build --locked --manifest-path "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli \
   170	    --bin callisto --target-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-build"
   171	  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-build/debug/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
   172	elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]] && fetch_prebuilt; then
   173	  echo "Callisto downloaded from GitHub Releases ($DOWNLOAD_URL)"
   174	elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
   175	  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io (latest)"
   176	  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
   177	elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --version "$CRATE_VERSION" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
   178	  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io ($CRATE_VERSION)"
   179	  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
   180	else
   181	  if [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]]; then
   182	    echo "::error::callisto $TAG_NAME is available neither as a prebuilt asset nor on crates.io"
   183	    exit 1
   184	  fi
   185	  echo "Installing from git source (crates.io install failed or was skipped)..."
   186	  cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git callisto-cli --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
   187	  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
   188	fi
   189	
   190	echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> $GITHUB_PATH
   191	if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
   192	  echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
   193	fi

     2	description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, moon and the .prototools toolchain, and Callisto CLI'
     3	inputs:
     4	  source:
     5	    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto installs the requested release version; local builds validated Callisto checkout source and ignores version. Release jobs must use local.'
     6	    required: false
     7	    default: 'auto'
     8	  version:
     9	    description: >-
    10	      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's
    11	      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
    12	      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    13	    required: false
    14	    default: 'latest'
    15	  verification:
    16	    description: >-
    17	      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
    18	      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml). One of: require = a failed
    19	      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
    20	      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never
    21	      run the unverified asset); skip = do not verify, warn, and use the asset. Releases built
    22	      before the first attested release carry no attestation, hence the fallback default.
    23	    required: false
    24	    default: 'fallback'
    25	
    26	runs:
    27	  using: 'composite'
    28	  steps:
    29	    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
    30	      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
    31	      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
    32	      with:
    33	        components: clippy,rustfmt
    34	        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
    35	        save-if: "true"
    36	      env:
    37	        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
    38	        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"
    39	
    40	    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
    41	      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
    42	      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
    43	      with:
    44	        auto-install: true
    45	
    46	    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
    47	      shell: bash
    48	      env:
    49	        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
    50	        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
    51	        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: ${{ inputs.verification }}
    52	        GITHUB_ACTION_REF: ${{ github.action_ref }}
    53	        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    54	      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/install-callisto.sh" # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.

# Implementation Review Evidence

Load only the evidence needed for the current review.

## Language rules

- Rust: load `shared/references/hazards/rust.md` and `shared/references/hazards/rust-boundaries.md` for defect checks; load `shared/references/architecture/rust.md` for semantic-model and architecture signals.
- TypeScript or JavaScript: load `shared/references/hazards/typescript.md` and `shared/references/hazards/typescript-boundaries.md` for defect checks; load `shared/references/architecture/typescript.md` for semantic-model and architecture signals.
- Python: load `shared/references/hazards/python.md` and `shared/references/hazards/python-boundaries.md` for defect checks; load `shared/references/architecture/python.md` for semantic-model and architecture signals.
- Go: load `shared/references/hazards/go.md` and `shared/references/hazards/go-boundaries.md` for defect checks; load `shared/references/architecture/go.md` for semantic-model and architecture signals.
- Other languages: perform the core review and record the missing language pack as a coverage gap.
- If the diff adds or changes comments, load `shared/references/authoring/comments.md`.

## Required evidence

- Scope: each change maps to the task or a required sibling repair.
- Behavior: tests prove specified outcomes rather than implementation shape.
- Verification: method choice, boundary coverage, environment assumptions, and external-state freshness follow `shared/references/verification/evidence.md`.
- Hazards: changed code does not introduce a language-specific violation.
- Siblings: the search covers matching syntax and candidate sites with equivalent domain behavior.
- Structure: repeated defects are assessed for a missing concept, state, operation, boundary, abstraction, invariant, or enforcement mechanism.

A taxonomy match is a search lead, not proof. Cite live code for every issue and structural assessment.

Output:
READ 0
READ 1

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Installs or builds the Callisto binary. Factored out of action.yml so
     3	# callisto-action's own environment setup can call it directly by path
     4	# (github.action_path has no ref-ambiguous `uses:` to resolve), instead of
     5	# duplicating this logic.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	
     8	# Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
     9	# tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
    10	# "git add -A").
    11	CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
    12	mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
    13	TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"
    14	SOURCE="$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    15	
    16	if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
    17	  echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
    18	  exit 1
    19	fi
    20	
    21	# With no explicit version override, install the release this action's own
    22	# invocation is pinned to (GITHUB_ACTION_REF, github.action_ref) rather than
    23	# whatever is newest, so `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` always
    24	# installs X.Y.Z. Falls back to true "latest" when the ref is unset (local or
    25	# unpinned invocation) or matches no published callisto@ tag.
    26	if [[ "$SOURCE" == "auto" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" && -n "${GITHUB_ACTION_REF:-}" ]]; then
    27	  resolved_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git 'callisto@*' 2>/dev/null \
    28	    | awk -v ref="$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" '$1 == ref { print $2 }' \
    29	    | sed -e 's#^refs/tags/##' -e 's/\^{}$//' \
    30	    | sort -V | tail -n1) || true
    31	  if [[ -n "$resolved_tag" ]]; then
    32	    echo "Resolved action ref $GITHUB_ACTION_REF to $resolved_tag"
    33	    TAG_NAME="$resolved_tag"
    34	  fi
    35	fi
    36	
    37	# Validate verification mode
    38	VERIFICATION="${INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION:-fallback}"
    39	case "$VERIFICATION" in
    40	  require|fallback|skip) ;;
    41	  *)
    42	    echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto verification '$VERIFICATION' (valid values: require, fallback, skip)"
    43	    exit 1
    44	    ;;
    45	esac
    46	
    47	# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
    48	OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    49	ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)
    50	
    51	if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
    52	  if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "arm64" ]]; then
    53	    ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
    54	  else
    55	    ASSET_NAME=""
    56	  fi
    57	elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == "linux" ]]; then
    58	  if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "x86_64" ]]; then
    59	    ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
    60	  else
    61	    ASSET_NAME=""
    62	  fi
    63	elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == *"mingw"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"msys"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"windows"* ]]; then
    64	  ASSET_NAME=""
    65	else
    66	  ASSET_NAME=""
    67	fi
    68	
    69	if [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]]; then
    70	  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/latest/download/$ASSET_NAME"
    71	elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]]; then
    72	  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/$TAG_NAME/$ASSET_NAME"
    73	fi
    74	
    75	# Derive a crates.io version spec from TAG_NAME: "latest" installs
    76	# whatever crates.io resolves as latest (no --version flag); an
    77	# explicit tag ("callisto@0.5.0" or legacy "callisto-cli@0.5.0")
    78	# strips either prefix down to the bare semver cargo install expects.

   101	# extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
   102	# returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.

# Rust Hazard Reference

Patterns are leads, not findings. Confirm a reachable bad outcome in live code and record evidence that rules out the plausible exception. Use `shared/references/hazards/rust-boundaries.md` for boundary taxonomies T7 and T10.

## T8 · False-success mutation

- Signal: a write-like function returns `Ok(())` before the required mutation or acknowledgment occurs.
- Search: write/update/set/publish functions and early `Ok` returns.
- Confirm: the caller cannot distinguish required work from a no-op and proceeds with incorrect state.
- Refute: idempotent success is part of the contract or the caller verifies the resulting state.

## T1 · Discarded input

- Signal: a meaningful public or trait parameter is renamed with `_`, dropped, or never reaches the behavior it configures.
- Confirm: a caller supplies a value whose omission changes the outcome.
- Refute: the signature is imposed by a trait or compatibility boundary and the value is intentionally irrelevant.

## T2 · Silent fallback

- Signal: `unwrap_or*` substitutes a default after parsing, lookup, or I/O failure.
- Confirm: the default hides a state the caller must distinguish.
- Refute: the default is the documented domain value and preserves required behavior.

## T3 · Recoverable panic

- Signal: `unwrap`, `expect`, or `panic!` is reachable in reusable code.
- Confirm: valid external input or a recoverable dependency failure reaches it.
- Refute: the path is an established invariant, test-only code, or process entrypoint policy.

## T4 · Lost error

- Signal: a `Result` is assigned to `_`, dropped, or replaced by success.
- Confirm: failure changes subsequent correctness and no owner observes it.
- Refute: best-effort behavior is explicit and the discarded failure has no required consequence.

## T5 · Arithmetic overflow

- Signal: user- or data-controlled integers participate in unchecked arithmetic near a bound.
- Confirm: a reachable value overflows under the relevant build profile.
- Refute: types, validation, or domain limits prove the operation safe.

## T6 · Unsafe contract gap

- Signal: an `unsafe` block lacks a locally checkable safety contract or relies on an unverified caller invariant.
- Confirm: a reachable input violates the invariant and can cause undefined behavior.
- Refute: the contract is enforced at the boundary and covers every operation in the block.

## T9 · Incomplete or ambiguous variants

- Signal: enum conversion uses a catch-all that rejects a valid variant, or diagnostic identifiers collide where consumers require uniqueness.
- Confirm: a current variant is mishandled or a consumer cannot distinguish outcomes.
- Refute: the source is intentionally open, the fallback is contractual, or duplicate identifiers are documented aliases.

Search broadly enough to find candidates, then cite the exact caller, input, state transition, and failure for every confirmed result.

# Rust Boundary Hazards · T7 and T10

Use this reference when tracing captured intent or error information across Rust boundaries. Record each hop; matching syntax alone cannot prove loss.

## T7 · Intent lost before execution

- Signal: a plan, config, request, or options value captures a meaningful field, but a narrower downstream signature or command omits it.
- Outcome: user intent is replaced by a default or never affects the side effect.
- Evidence: identify the construction site, field value, call chain, final execution boundary, and the first hop where the value disappears.
- Refute: the field is read by an equivalent owner, intentionally ignored under a documented mode, or cannot change the selected operation.

Candidate search:

- Start from user-controlled fields and domain state, not a fixed list of names.
- Compare constructed fields with downstream parameters, command arguments, serialized payloads, and storage writes.
- Treat an unused field as confirmable only when a reachable caller supplies a value that should change behavior.

## T10 · Error context lost across a boundary

- Signal: `map_err`, string conversion, or a replacement error discards the source, diagnostic identity, span, retryability, or structured fields.
- Outcome: the caller cannot make a required decision or diagnose the underlying failure.
- Evidence: compare the source error's useful capabilities with the destination error and show which required information no longer survives.
- Refute: the destination boundary accepts only a string or stable wire shape, sensitive detail must be removed, or the lost data has no consumer.

Distinguish T10 from T4: T4 leaves a failure unowned; T10 reports a failure through a representation that may be too weak. Preserve only the context the destination reader or machine consumer needs.

# Verification Evidence

Choose evidence from the changed risk and the workspace's available capabilities. Do not run every method by default.

## Method selection

- Examples: bounded behavior with clear representative cases.
- Property or fuzz testing: parsers, combinatorial inputs, state transitions, graph logic, or round trips. Name the generated domain and a meaningful oracle or invariant; a no-panic check alone rarely proves behavior.
- Mutation or deliberate fault: show that tests distinguish an important wrong implementation from the intended one.
- Boundary testing: exercise the contract implicated by the change. Name any mocked segment and why the remaining boundary is sufficient.
- Environment testing: exercise only environment assumptions that can change the outcome, such as runtime version, PATH, working directory, build tags, packaging, or CI configuration.

Prefer project-configured commands and installed tools. A missing optional tool is a coverage gap, not permission to install it or fabricate a result.

## Evidence quality

Record the claim, actual command or inspection, observed result, and remaining gap. Generated tests also record the generator and oracle. External state records an immutable identity and observation time when it affects the decision.

A test discriminates behavior when a controlled mutation, deliberate fault, isolated prior revision, or equivalent evidence makes it fail for the relevant wrong behavior and pass for the corrected behavior. Do not modify shared worktrees or user state merely to manufacture a red run.

Before completion, every started verification task has a terminal result that was read, or is explicitly excluded from the verified scope.

# Rust Architecture Smells

## Outcome

Use confirmed findings to ask whether the codebase lacks one domain concept, state, operation, boundary, invariant, or enforcement mechanism. A smell is an architecture lead, not proof and not a predetermined trait design.

## Signals

- Structural equality is used where the domain exposes a broader predicate such as `matches`, `satisfies`, or `equivalent`.
- Related values and validity flags can represent contradictory states instead of one enum or result type.
- Several callers reconstruct the same command, mutation, transition, or error mapping.
- Multi-step filesystem or repository mutation has no owner for atomicity, rollback, or durability.
- Producer and consumer representations can lose formatting, aliases, variants, or fields across serialization.
- Traversal, retry, or fixpoint logic has no explicit bound or termination condition.
- User-provided metadata is replaced by defaults between capture and execution.
- User-visible or serialized collections have unstable order when the contract requires deterministic output.
- Tests hand-build serialized fixtures that can drift from the production representation.
- An architectural rule exists only in prose, with no type, test, lint, or CI enforcement.

## Refutation

Read the live callers, ownership boundaries, public contracts, and persisted architecture model. Dismiss or narrow the signal when behavior is intentionally local, the state cannot diverge, the boundary already has one owner, or the repository explicitly permits the variation.

Performance shapes such as allocation strategy are architecture concerns only with measurements or a documented hot-path constraint. Public documentation and collection choices follow the target repository's policy, not this reference.

GUIDANCE 0

# Rust Hazard Reference

Patterns are leads, not findings. Confirm a reachable bad outcome in live code and record evidence that rules out the plausible exception. Use `shared/references/hazards/rust-boundaries.md` for boundary taxonomies T7 and T10.

## T8 · False-success mutation

- Signal: a write-like function returns `Ok(())` before the required mutation or acknowledgment occurs.
- Search: write/update/set/publish functions and early `Ok` returns.
- Confirm: the caller cannot distinguish required work from a no-op and proceeds with incorrect state.
- Refute: idempotent success is part of the contract or the caller verifies the resulting state.

## T1 · Discarded input

- Signal: a meaningful public or trait parameter is renamed with `_`, dropped, or never reaches the behavior it configures.
- Confirm: a caller supplies a value whose omission changes the outcome.
- Refute: the signature is imposed by a trait or compatibility boundary and the value is intentionally irrelevant.

## T2 · Silent fallback

- Signal: `unwrap_or*` substitutes a default after parsing, lookup, or I/O failure.
- Confirm: the default hides a state the caller must distinguish.
- Refute: the default is the documented domain value and preserves required behavior.

## T3 · Recoverable panic

- Signal: `unwrap`, `expect`, or `panic!` is reachable in reusable code.
- Confirm: valid external input or a recoverable dependency failure reaches it.
- Refute: the path is an established invariant, test-only code, or process entrypoint policy.

## T4 · Lost error

- Signal: a `Result` is assigned to `_`, dropped, or replaced by success.
- Confirm: failure changes subsequent correctness and no owner observes it.
- Refute: best-effort behavior is explicit and the discarded failure has no required consequence.

## T5 · Arithmetic overflow

- Signal: user- or data-controlled integers participate in unchecked arithmetic near a bound.
- Confirm: a reachable value overflows under the relevant build profile.
- Refute: types, validation, or domain limits prove the operation safe.

## T6 · Unsafe contract gap

- Signal: an `unsafe` block lacks a locally checkable safety contract or relies on an unverified caller invariant.
- Confirm: a reachable input violates the invariant and can cause undefined behavior.
- Refute: the contract is enforced at the boundary and covers every operation in the block.

## T9 · Incomplete or ambiguous variants

- Signal: enum conversion uses a catch-all that rejects a valid variant, or diagnostic identifiers collide where consumers require uniqueness.
- Confirm: a current variant is mishandled or a consumer cannot distinguish outcomes.
- Refute: the source is intentionally open, the fallback is contractual, or duplicate identifiers are documented aliases.

Search broadly enough to find candidates, then cite the exact caller, input, state transition, and failure for every confirmed result.
GUIDANCE 1

# Rust Boundary Hazards · T7 and T10

Use this reference when tracing captured intent or error information across Rust boundaries. Record each hop; matching syntax alone cannot prove loss.

## T7 · Intent lost before execution

- Signal: a plan, config, request, or options value captures a meaningful field, but a narrower downstream signature or command omits it.
- Outcome: user intent is replaced by a default or never affects the side effect.
- Evidence: identify the construction site, field value, call chain, final execution boundary, and the first hop where the value disappears.
- Refute: the field is read by an equivalent owner, intentionally ignored under a documented mode, or cannot change the selected operation.

Candidate search:

- Start from user-controlled fields and domain state, not a fixed list of names.
- Compare constructed fields with downstream parameters, command arguments, serialized payloads, and storage writes.
- Treat an unused field as confirmable only when a reachable caller supplies a value that should change behavior.

## T10 · Error context lost across a boundary

- Signal: `map_err`, string conversion, or a replacement error discards the source, diagnostic identity, span, retryability, or structured fields.
- Outcome: the caller cannot make a required decision or diagnose the underlying failure.
- Evidence: compare the source error's useful capabilities with the destination error and show which required information no longer survives.
- Refute: the destination boundary accepts only a string or stable wire shape, sensitive detail must be removed, or the lost data has no consumer.

# Verification Evidence

Choose evidence from the changed risk and the workspace's available capabilities. Do not run every method by default.

## Method selection

- Examples: bounded behavior with clear representative cases.
- Property or fuzz testing: parsers, combinatorial inputs, state transitions, graph logic, or round trips. Name the generated domain and a meaningful oracle or invariant; a no-panic check alone rarely proves behavior.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
     3	# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
     4	#
     5	# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
     6	# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
     7	# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
     8	# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
     9	# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
    10	# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
    11	# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
    12	# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
    13	# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
    14	set -euo pipefail
    15	
    16	cd "$INPUT_CWD"
    17	
    18	# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
    19	# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
    20	# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
    21	# commit API, on the staging branch.
    22	base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    23	
    24	release_pr_snapshot() {
    25	  local raw_prs
    26	  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
    27	  jq -cn \
    28	    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    29	    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    30	    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    31	    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    32	    '{
    33	      schemaVersion: 2,
    34	      repository: $repository,
    35	      baseBranch: $base_branch,
    36	      baseCommit: $base_commit,
    37	      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
    38	        number,
    39	        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
    40	        headBranch: .headRefName,
    41	        headCommit: .headRefOid
    42	      }]
    43	    }'
    44	}
    45	
    46	snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
    47	decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
    48	  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
    49	  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    50	  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    51	  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
    52	decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
    53	
    54	case "$decision_kind" in

item.stdout:
1	//! Typed, provider-neutral decisions for a managed release pull request.
     2	//!
     3	//! This is deliberately pre-merge collaboration policy, rather than durable
     4	//! release authority. The values name a narrow, credential-free observation
     5	//! and the one forge mutation sequence that an executor may perform.
     6	//!
     7	//! The executor never pushes Git objects directly: on a public repository,
     8	//! GitHub's automatic `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write to `.github/workflows/*`
     9	//! through the Git push protocol or through the forge commit API's own
    10	//! `fileChanges`, on any ref. The managed branch is instead updated by
    11	//! committing only non-workflow changes onto a deterministic staging branch
    12	//! rooted at the current base commit (so it inherits the base's current
    13	//! workflow content without writing to that path at all), then moving the
    14	//! managed branch's ref onto that commit -- a ref update is not itself a
    15	//! write to `.github/workflows/*` and is not subject to the restriction.
    16	
    17	use base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD as BASE64;
    18	use base64::Engine as _;
    19	use schemars::JsonSchema;
    20	use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize};
    21	
    22	use crate::{CommitSha, GitHubRepository};
    23	
    24	/// Explicit identity and presentation configuration for one managed release PR.
    25	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
    26	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]
    27	pub struct ReleasePrConfigV1 {
    28	    pub schema_version: u8,
    29	    pub repository: GitHubRepository,
    30	    pub base_branch: String,
    31	    pub release_branch: String,
    32	}
    33	
    34	impl ReleasePrConfigV1 {
    35	    pub const SCHEMA_VERSION: u8 = 1;
    36	
    37	    pub fn new(
    38	        repository: GitHubRepository,
    39	        base_branch: String,
    40	        release_branch: String,
    41	    ) -> Result<Self, ReleasePrDecisionError> {
    42	        validate_branch("base branch", &base_branch)?;
    43	        validate_branch("managed release branch", &release_branch)?;
    44	        Ok(Self {
    45	            schema_version: Self::SCHEMA_VERSION,
    46	            repository,
    47	            base_branch,
    48	            release_branch,
    49	        })
    50	    }
    51	
    52	    /// The deterministic staging branch this config's release branch commits
    53	    /// through before any managed-branch ref is moved.
    54	    pub fn staging_branch(&self) -> String {
    55	        format!("{}--staging", self.release_branch)
    56	    }
    57	}
    58	
    59	/// The on-the-wire shape of [`ReleasePrConfigV1`], before its invariants are checked.
    60	///
    61	/// Deserializing this (rather than `ReleasePrConfigV1` itself) then calling
    62	/// [`ReleasePrConfigV1::from_wire`] keeps a caller's own typed
    63	/// [`ReleasePrDecisionError`] (e.g. `E142`) intact -- deserializing straight into
    64	/// `ReleasePrConfigV1` still validates, but folds a validation failure into a generic
    65	/// `serde` string error, losing the code.
    66	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
    67	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]
    68	pub struct ReleasePrConfigWireV1 {
    69	    pub schema_version: u8,
    70	    pub repository: GitHubRepository,
    71	    pub base_branch: String,
    72	    pub release_branch: String,
    73	}
    74	
    75	impl ReleasePrConfigV1 {
    76	    /// Validates an already-parsed wire value into a well-formed config.
    77	    pub fn from_wire(wire: ReleasePrConfigWireV1) -> Result<Self, ReleasePrDecisionError> {
    78	        check_schema_version(wire.schema_version, Self::SCHEMA_VERSION, "release PR configuration")?;
    79	        Self::new(wire.repository, wire.base_branch, wire.release_branch)
    80	    }

   225	    /// Derives the only permitted action from fresh workspace and forge facts.
   226	    pub fn derive(
   227	        has_pending_changesets: bool,
   228	        config: &ReleasePrConfigV1,
   229	        snapshot: &ReleasePrSnapshotV2,
   230	    ) -> Result<Self, ReleasePrDecisionError> {
   231	        if snapshot.repository != config.repository || snapshot.base_branch != config.base_branch {
   232	            return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::SnapshotIdentityMismatch);
   233	        }
   234	
   235	        let staging_branch = config.staging_branch();
   236	        let mut eligible = Vec::new();
   237	        for pr in &snapshot.open_pull_requests {
   238	            if pr.head_branch == staging_branch {
   239	                return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::StagingBranchPullRequest { number: pr.number });
   240	            }
   241	            let shape = managed_branch_shape(&config.release_branch, &pr.head_branch)?;
   242	            if shape.is_some() {
   243	                if pr.head_repository != config.repository {
   244	                    return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::ForeignManagedPullRequest {
   245	                        number: pr.number,
   246	                        repository: pr.head_repository.clone(),
   247	                    });
   248	                }
   249	                eligible.push(pr);
   250	            }
   251	        }
   252	        if eligible.len() > 1 {
   253	            return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::AmbiguousManagedPullRequests { count: eligible.len() });
   254	        }

   257	            ReleasePrActionV2::Noop {
   258	                reason: ReleasePrNoopReasonV1::NoPendingChangesets,
   259	            }

   261	            ReleasePrActionV2::Update {
   262	                pull_request_number: pr.number,
   263	                branch: pr.head_branch.clone(),
   264	                expected_head_commit: pr.head_commit.clone(),
   265	                staging_branch: staging_branch.clone(),
   266	            }
   267	        } else {
   268	            ReleasePrActionV2::Create {
   269	                branch: config.release_branch.clone(),
   270	                staging_branch,
   271	            }
   272	        };

   274	            schema_version: Self::SCHEMA_VERSION,
   275	            config: config.clone(),
   276	            snapshot: snapshot.clone(),
   277	            action,
   278	        })
   279	    }

   441	fn validate_branch(kind: &'static str, branch: &str) -> Result<(), ReleasePrDecisionError> {
   442	    let valid = !branch.is_empty()
   443	        && !branch.starts_with('-')
   444	        && !branch.starts_with('/')
   445	        && !branch.ends_with('/')
   446	        && !branch.contains("//")
   447	        && !branch.contains("..")
   448	        && !branch.contains("@{")
   449	        && branch != "@"
   450	        && branch
   451	            .split('/')
   452	            .all(|part| !part.starts_with('.') && !part.ends_with(".lock"))
   453	        && branch.chars().all(|ch| {
   454	            !ch.is_ascii_control() && !ch.is_whitespace() && !matches!(ch, '~' | '^' | ':' | '?' | '*' | '[' | '\\')
   455	        });
   456	    if valid {
   457	        Ok(())
   458	    } else {
   459	        Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::InvalidBranch {
   460	            kind,
   461	            branch: branch.to_string(),
   462	        })
   463	    }
   464	}

   466	fn managed_branch_shape(canonical: &str, branch: &str) -> Result<Option<()>, ReleasePrDecisionError> {
   467	    if branch == canonical {
   468	        return Ok(Some(()));
   469	    }
   470	    let Some(suffix) = branch.strip_prefix(&format!("{canonical}--")) else {
   471	        return Ok(None);
   472	    };
   473	    if suffix.len() == 40
   474	        && suffix
   475	            .bytes()
   476	            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(byte, b'a'..=b'f'))
   477	    {
   478	        Ok(Some(()))
   479	    } else {
   480	        Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::MalformedManagedBranch {
   481	            branch: branch.to_string(),
   482	        })
   483	    }
   484	}

   563	    /// paths, an empty change set, or a payload over [`MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES`].
   564	    pub fn from_changes(

   573	        }
   574	
   575	        let mut additions = Vec::new();
   576	        let mut deletions = Vec::new();
   577	        let mut total_content_bytes = 0usize;

   580	            validate_commit_plan_path(&change.path)?;
   581	            match change.kind {
   582	                StagedChangeKindV1::Added | StagedChangeKindV1::Modified => {
   583	                    let mode = change.new_mode.unwrap_or(REGULAR_FILE_MODE);

   586	                            path: change.path,
   587	                            mode,
   588	                        });
   589	                    }
   590	                    let contents = change.contents.unwrap_or_default();
   591	                    total_content_bytes += contents.len();
   592	                    additions.push(ReleasePrFileAdditionV1 {
   593	                        path: change.path,
   594	                        contents_base64: BASE64.encode(contents),
   595	                    });
   596	                }

   598	                    deletions.push(ReleasePrFileDeletionV1 { path: change.path });
   599	                }
   600	                StagedChangeKindV1::Renamed
   601	                | StagedChangeKindV1::Copied
   602	                | StagedChangeKindV1::TypeChanged
   603	                | StagedChangeKindV1::Unmerged => {
   604	                    return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::UnsupportedChangeKind {
   605	                        path: change.path,
   606	                        kind: change.kind,
   607	                    });

   614	                bytes: total_content_bytes,
   615	                limit: MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES,
   616	            });
   617	        }

   619	        Ok(Self {
   620	            schema_version: Self::SCHEMA_VERSION,

   723	fn validate_commit_plan_path(path: &str) -> Result<(), ReleasePrDecisionError> {
   724	    let forbidden = path.is_empty()
   725	        || path.starts_with('/')
   726	        || path.starts_with(".github/workflows/")
   727	        || path == ".github/workflows"
   728	        || path.starts_with(".git/")
   729	        || path == ".git"
   730	        || path.split('/').any(|part| part == "..")
   731	        || path.contains('\0');
   732	    if forbidden {
   733	        Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::ForbiddenCommitPlanPath { path: path.to_string() })
   734	    } else {
   735	        Ok(())
   736	    }
   737	}

   443	        && !branch.starts_with('-')
   444	        && !branch.starts_with('/')
   445	        && !branch.ends_with('/')
   446	        && !branch.contains("//")
   447	        && !branch.contains("..")
   448	        && !branch.contains("@{")
   449	        && branch != "@"
   450	        && branch
   451	            .split('/')
   452	            .all(|part| !part.starts_with('.') && !part.ends_with(".lock"))
   453	        && branch.chars().all(|ch| {
   454	            !ch.is_ascii_control() && !ch.is_whitespace() && !matches!(ch, '~' | '^' | ':' | '?' | '*' | '[' | '\\')

   457	        Ok(())
   458	    } else {

   547	pub struct ReleasePrCommitPlanV1 {
   548	    pub schema_version: u8,
   549	    pub base_commit: CommitSha,
   550	    pub message: String,

   556	impl ReleasePrCommitPlanV1 {
   557	    pub const SCHEMA_VERSION: u8 = 1;
   558	
   559	    /// Builds a commit plan from a Git index diff. Fails closed on anything
   560	    /// the forge commit API cannot faithfully express or that must never
   561	    /// cross this boundary: non-regular file modes, renames/copies/type
   562	    /// changes/unmerged paths, `.github/workflows/*` (and other unsafe)
   563	    /// paths, an empty change set, or a payload over [`MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES`].
   564	    pub fn from_changes(
   565	        base_commit: CommitSha,
   566	        message: String,
   567	        changes: Vec<StagedChangeV1>,
   568	    ) -> Result<Self, ReleasePrDecisionError> {
   569	        if changes.is_empty() {
   570	            return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::EmptyCommitPlan {
   571	                base_commit: base_commit.as_str().to_string(),
   572	            });
   573	        }
   574	
   575	        let mut additions = Vec::new();
   576	        let mut deletions = Vec::new();
   577	        let mut total_content_bytes = 0usize;
   578	
   579	        for change in changes {
   580	            validate_commit_plan_path(&change.path)?;
   581	            match change.kind {
   582	                StagedChangeKindV1::Added | StagedChangeKindV1::Modified => {
   583	                    let mode = change.new_mode.unwrap_or(REGULAR_FILE_MODE);
   584	                    if mode != REGULAR_FILE_MODE {
   585	                        return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::UnsupportedFileMode {
   586	                            path: change.path,
   587	                            mode,
   588	                        });
   589	                    }
   590	                    let contents = change.contents.unwrap_or_default();
   591	                    total_content_bytes += contents.len();
   592	                    additions.push(ReleasePrFileAdditionV1 {
   593	                        path: change.path,
   594	                        contents_base64: BASE64.encode(contents),
   595	                    });
   596	                }
   597	                StagedChangeKindV1::Deleted => {
   598	                    deletions.push(ReleasePrFileDeletionV1 { path: change.path });
   599	                }
   600	                StagedChangeKindV1::Renamed
   601	                | StagedChangeKindV1::Copied
   602	                | StagedChangeKindV1::TypeChanged
   603	                | StagedChangeKindV1::Unmerged => {
   604	                    return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::UnsupportedChangeKind {
   605	                        path: change.path,
   606	                        kind: change.kind,
   607	                    });
   608	                }
   609	            }
   610	        }
   611	
   612	        if total_content_bytes > MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES {
   613	            return Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::CommitPlanTooLarge {
   614	                bytes: total_content_bytes,
   615	                limit: MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES,
   616	            });
   617	        }
   618	
   619	        Ok(Self {
   620	            schema_version: Self::SCHEMA_VERSION,
   621	            base_commit,
   622	            message,
   623	            additions,
   624	            deletions,
   625	            total_content_bytes,
   626	        })
   627	    }
   628	}

   723	fn validate_commit_plan_path(path: &str) -> Result<(), ReleasePrDecisionError> {
   724	    let forbidden = path.is_empty()
   725	        || path.starts_with('/')
   726	        || path.starts_with(".github/workflows/")
   727	        || path == ".github/workflows"
   728	        || path.starts_with(".git/")
   729	        || path == ".git"
   730	        || path.split('/').any(|part| part == "..")
   731	        || path.contains('\0');
   732	    if forbidden {
   733	        Err(ReleasePrDecisionError::ForbiddenCommitPlanPath { path: path.to_string() })
   734	    } else {
   735	        Ok(())
   736	    }
   737	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
     3	# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
     4	#
     5	# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
     6	# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
     7	# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
     8	# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
     9	# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
    10	# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
    11	# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
    12	# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
    13	# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
    14	set -euo pipefail
    15	
    16	cd "$INPUT_CWD"
    17	
    18	# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
    19	# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
    20	# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
    21	# commit API, on the staging branch.
    22	base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    23	
    24	release_pr_snapshot() {
    25	  local raw_prs
    26	  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
    27	  jq -cn \
    28	    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    29	    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    30	    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    31	    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    32	    '{
    33	      schemaVersion: 2,
    34	      repository: $repository,
    35	      baseBranch: $base_branch,
    36	      baseCommit: $base_commit,
    37	      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
    38	        number,
    39	        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
    40	        headBranch: .headRefName,
    41	        headCommit: .headRefOid
    42	      }]
    43	    }'
    44	}
    45	
    46	snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
    47	decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
    48	  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
    49	  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    50	  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    51	  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
    52	decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
    53	
    54	case "$decision_kind" in
    55	  noop)
    56	    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    57	    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    58	    exit 0
    59	    ;;
    60	  create)
    61	    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    62	    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    63	    existing_pr=''
    64	    ;;
    65	  update)
    66	    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    67	    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    68	    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    69	    ;;
    70	  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
    71	esac
    72	
    73	echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    74	if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
    75	  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
    76	  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
    77	else
    78	  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
    79	fi
    80	
    81	read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
    82	command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH")
    83	"${command[@]}"
    84	git add -A
    85	test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }
    86	
    87	plan_file=$(mktemp)
    88	callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
    89	local_tree=$(git write-tree)
    90	
    91	staging_created=false
    92	cleanup_staging() {
    93	  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    94	    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
    95	      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
    96	  fi
    97	  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
    98	}
    99	trap cleanup_staging EXIT
   100	
   101	# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
   102	# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
   103	# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
   104	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
   105	
   106	if gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
   107	  :
   108	else
   109	  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
   110	fi
   111	staging_created=true
   112	
   113	jq -n \
   114	  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
   115	  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
   116	  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
   117	  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
   118	  '{
   119	    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
   120	    variables: {
   121	      input: {
   122	        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
   123	        message: {headline: $headline},
   124	        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
   125	        fileChanges: {
   126	          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
   127	          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
   128	        }
   129	      }
   130	    }
   131	  }' > body.json
   132	
   133	new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
   134	remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
   135	if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
   136	  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
   137	  exit 1
   138	fi
   139	
   140	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
   141	
   142	if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
   143	  gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
   144	else
   145	  if ! gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
   146	    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
   147	  fi
   148	fi
   149	moved_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
   150	if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
   151	  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
   152	  exit 1
   153	fi
   154	
   155	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
   156	
   157	label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
   158	if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
   159	  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
   160	fi
   161	
   162	case "$decision_kind" in
   163	  create)
   164	    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
   165	    ;;
   166	  update)
   167	    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
   168	    ;;
   169	esac

using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Validate mode
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_MODE: ${{ inputs.mode }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/validate-mode.sh"
    # setup-callisto's own steps, called directly rather than through its
    # `uses:` (both `$/` and an external owner/repo/path@ref resolve against
    # whichever ref invoked *this* action, not necessarily a real one -- see
    # setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh's header). github.action_path
    # is this action's own checked-out directory, so a sibling-relative path
    # always uses the same ref this action itself was invoked at.
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"
    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true
    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: auto
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: fallback
        GITHUB_ACTION_REF: ${{ github.action_ref }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github_token || github.token }}
      run: bash "${{ github.action_path }}/../setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh" # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
    - name: Create or update release PR
      id: version-pr
      if: inputs.mode == 'version-pr'
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.version_command }}
        INPUT_DECISION_PATH: ${{ inputs.decision_path }}
        INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE: ${{ inputs.commit_message }}
        INPUT_TITLE: ${{ inputs.title }}
        INPUT_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.pr_label }}
        INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER: ${{ inputs.setup_git_user }}
        INPUT_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch }}
        INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.release_branch }}
        INPUT_CWD: ${{ inputs.cwd }}
        # GitHub exposes the installation token as a context, not a guaranteed
        # inherited environment variable. Using the context also works for the
        # repository workflow that invokes this action after checkout.
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github_token || github.token }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh"
    - name: Run release
      id: release

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
     3	# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
     4	#
     5	# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
     6	# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
     7	# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
     8	# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
     9	# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
    10	# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
    11	# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
    12	# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
    13	# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
    14	set -euo pipefail
    15	
    16	cd "$INPUT_CWD"
    17	
    18	# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
    19	# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
    20	# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
    21	# commit API, on the staging branch.
    22	base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    23	
    24	release_pr_snapshot() {
    25	  local raw_prs
    26	  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
    27	  jq -cn \
    28	    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    29	    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    30	    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    31	    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    32	    '{
    33	      schemaVersion: 2,
    34	      repository: $repository,
    35	      baseBranch: $base_branch,
    36	      baseCommit: $base_commit,
    37	      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
    38	        number,
    39	        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
    40	        headBranch: .headRefName,
    41	        headCommit: .headRefOid
    42	      }]
    43	    }'
    44	}
    45	
    46	snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
    47	decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
    48	  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
    49	  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    50	  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    51	  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")

   253	def handoff_roundtrip_errors(jobs):
   254	    """Run the plan job's checksum line, move the files to another directory as a
   255	    different runner would, and run the build job's verify line against them."""
   256	    def step_run(job, name):
   257	        for s in jobs.get(job, {}).get("steps", []):
   258	            if s.get("name") == name:
   259	                return s.get("run", "")
   260	        return ""

   262	    def pick(script, *needles):
   263	        hits = [ln.strip() for ln in script.splitlines() if all(n in ln for n in needles)]
   264	        return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None
   265	
   266	    write = pick(step_run("plan", "Derive and hash intent"), "shasum -a 256", ".sha256", ">")
   267	    verify = pick(step_run("build-artifact", "Verify handoff"), "shasum -a 256 -c")
   268	    if not write or not verify:
   269	        return ["handoff checksum write/verify lines could not be located for the round-trip check"]
   270	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
   271	        src, dst = os.path.join(tmp, "plan-runner", "release-intent"), os.path.join(tmp, "build-runner", "release-intent")

   273	        os.makedirs(dst)
   274	        with open(os.path.join(src, "release-intent.json"), "w") as f:
   275	            f.write('{"schemaVersion":3}\n')
   276	        subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", "set -euo pipefail; " + write], check=True, env={**os.environ, "handoff_dir": src})

   278	            shutil.copy(os.path.join(src, n), os.path.join(dst, n))
   279	        shutil.rmtree(src)
   280	        r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", "set -euo pipefail; " + verify], env={**os.environ, "handoff_dir": dst}, capture_output=True, text=True)
   281	    if r.returncode != 0:
   282	        return ["intent checksum written by plan does not verify from a different directory (absolute path recorded?)"]
   283	    return []

   286	def slots_probe_errors(jobs):

   288	    has_artifacts matches neither downstream guard, so every later job skips on a green run."""
   289	    script = next((s.get("run", "") for s in jobs.get("plan", {}).get("steps", []) if s.get("id") == "slots"), "")

   292	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:

   295	        env = {**os.environ, "RUNNER_TEMP": os.path.join(tmp, "absent"), "GITHUB_OUTPUT": out}
   296	        result = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)

   438	    errs = []
   439	    try:

   441	        with open(paths["config"], "rb") as f:
   442	            declared = tomllib.load(f).get("release", {}).get("artifact", [])
   443	        rust = {(a["target"], a["asset-name"]) for a in declared}
   444	    except ImportError:  # python < 3.11: read the artifact tables by text
   445	        text = open(paths["config"]).read()
   446	        rust = set(re.findall(r'target\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\nasset-name\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', text))
   447	    if not rust:
   448	        return [f"{paths['config']}: no [[release.artifact]] target/asset-name pairs found"]
   449	    rust_assets = {a for _, a in rust}
   450	
   451	    def compare(label, found):
   452	        for t, a in sorted(rust - found):
   453	            errs.append(f"{label}: missing ({t}, {a}) declared in {paths['config']}")
   454	        for t, a in sorted(found - rust):
   455	            errs.append(f"{label}: ({t}, {a}) disagrees with {paths['config']}")
   456	
   457	    compare(f"{paths['release']} build-artifact matrix", matrix_pairs(paths["release"], "build-artifact"))
   458	    ci = load(paths["ci"])
   459	    ci_pairs = set()
   460	    for job in ci["jobs"].values():

   462	            if "target" in e and "asset" in e:
   463	                ci_pairs.add((e["target"], e["asset"]))
   464	    compare(f"{paths['ci']} preflight matrix", ci_pairs)
   465	    script = open(paths["script"]).read()
   466	    compare(f"{paths['script']} tuples", set(re.findall(r"^\s*\w+:([^:\s]+):([^\s|\\)]+)[\s|\\)]*$", script, re.M)))

   468	    for asset in set(re.findall(r'ASSET_NAME="([^"]+)"', installer)):
   469	        if asset not in rust_assets:
   470	            errs.append(f"{paths['installer']}: asset {asset} disagrees with {paths['config']}")

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Regression test for the download/extraction format dispatch in
     3	# scripts/install-callisto.sh. Extracts the actual script body by a real
     4	# text anchor -- the "# Validate verification mode" comment through the end
     5	# of the file -- so this test always exercises the file's current real
     6	# logic; it cannot silently drift from it.
     7	#
     8	# Version resolution is covered separately; these fixtures supply the resolved tag.
     9	set -u
    10	ACTION_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    11	ACTION_YML="$ACTION_DIR/action.yml"
    12	INSTALL_SCRIPT="$ACTION_DIR/scripts/install-callisto.sh"
    13	
    14	extract_snippet() {
    15	  sed -n '/# Validate verification mode/,$p' "$INSTALL_SCRIPT"
    16	}
    17	
    18	# Runs the extracted snippet with uname/curl stubbed per test case, and
    19	# tar/unzip/cargo/cp always stubbed to record invocations into calls_file.
    20	# GITHUB_WORKSPACE points at an empty temp dir (no Cargo.toml present, so the
    21	# local-monorepo-build branch is always skipped here) and RUNNER_TEMP /
    22	# CALLISTO_BIN_DIR / GITHUB_PATH point at temp paths.
    23	run_case() {
    24	  local uname_s="$1"
    25	  local uname_m="$2"
    26	  local curl_exit="$3"
    27	  local gh_mode="${4:-ok}"
    28	  local mode="${5-}"
    29	  local tag="${6:-latest}"
    30	  local calls_file workspace runner_temp bin_dir github_path tmp_script
    31	  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
    32	  workspace="$(mktemp -d)"
    33	  runner_temp="$(mktemp -d)"
    34	  bin_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
    35	  github_path="$(mktemp)"
    36	  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
    37	  local isolated_path
    38	  isolated_path="$(mktemp -d)"
    39	  for t in tr grep rm; do ln -s "$(command -v "$t")" "$isolated_path/$t"; done
    40	  {
    41	    printf 'uname() {\n'
    42	    printf '  case "$1" in\n'
    43	    printf '    -s) echo %q ;;\n' "$uname_s"
    44	    printf '    -m) echo %q ;;\n' "$uname_m"
    45	    printf '    *) return 99 ;;\n'
    46	    printf '  esac\n'
    47	    printf '}\n'
    48	    printf 'curl() { echo "curl $*" >> %q; [[ %q -eq 0 ]] && : > "${@: -1}"; return %q; }\n' "$calls_file" "$curl_exit" "$curl_exit"
    49	    printf 'tar() { echo "tar $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    50	    printf 'unzip() { echo "unzip $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    51	    printf 'cargo() { echo "cargo $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    52	    printf 'cp() { echo "cp $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    53	    printf 'git() { echo "unexpected git $*" >> %q; return 99; }\n' "$calls_file"
    54	    case "$gh_mode" in
    55	      ok) printf 'gh() { echo "gh $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file" ;;
    56	      fail) printf 'gh() { echo "gh $*" >> %q; return 1; }\n' "$calls_file" ;;
    57	      missing) printf 'PATH=%q\n' "$isolated_path" ;;
    58	    esac
    59	    [[ -n "$mode" ]] && printf 'INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION=%q\n' "$mode"
    60	    printf 'GITHUB_WORKSPACE=%q\n' "$workspace"
    61	    printf 'RUNNER_TEMP=%q\n' "$runner_temp"
    62	    printf 'CALLISTO_BIN_DIR=%q\n' "$bin_dir"
    63	    printf 'GITHUB_PATH=%q\n' "$github_path"
    64	    printf 'TAG_NAME=%q\n' "$tag"
    65	    printf 'SOURCE=auto\n'
    66	    extract_snippet
    67	  } > "$tmp_script"
    68	  bash "$tmp_script"
    69	  local code=$?
    70	  [[ -e "$runner_temp/callisto.tar.gz" ]] && echo "ASSET_PRESENT"
    71	  echo "---CALLS---"
    72	  cat "$calls_file"
    73	  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file" "$github_path"
    74	  rm -rf "$workspace" "$runner_temp" "$bin_dir" "$isolated_path"
    75	  return $code
    76	}
    77	
    78	fail=0
    79	
    80	# 1. Windows is not a supported product-binary target. It must skip a
    81	# fictitious download and use the established installation fallback.
    82	out=$(run_case "MINGW64_NT-10.0" "x86_64" 0); code=$?
    83	if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
    84	  || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]] \
    85	  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]] \
    86	  || [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli"* ]]; then
    87	  echo "FAIL test_windows_falls_back_without_fictitious_asset: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
    88	else
    89	  echo "PASS test_windows_falls_back_without_fictitious_asset"
    90	fi
    91	
    92	# 2. macOS arm64 regression -> unchanged tar.gz behavior, unzip not invoked.
    93	out=$(run_case "Darwin" "arm64" 0); code=$?
    94	if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
    95	  || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "* ]] \
    96	  || [[ "$out" != *" -C "* ]] \
    97	  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]]; then
    98	  echo "FAIL test_macos_arm64_still_uses_targz: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
    99	else
   100	  echo "PASS test_macos_arm64_still_uses_targz"
   101	fi
   102	
   103	# 3. Linux amd64 regression -> unchanged tar.gz behavior, unzip not invoked.
   104	out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0); code=$?
   105	if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
   106	  || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "* ]] \
   107	  || [[ "$out" != *" -C "* ]] \
   108	  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]]; then
   109	  echo "FAIL test_linux_amd64_still_uses_targz: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   110	else
   111	  echo "PASS test_linux_amd64_still_uses_targz"
   112	fi
   113	
   114	# 4. Unknown/exotic OS must likewise use the fallback chain rather than
   115	# guessing an archive target.
   116	out=$(run_case "SunOS" "sun4u" 0); code=$?
   117	if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
   118	  || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf "* ]] \
   119	  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]] \
   120	  || [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli"* ]]; then
   121	  echo "FAIL test_unknown_os_uses_install_fallback: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   122	else
   123	  echo "PASS test_unknown_os_uses_install_fallback"
   124	fi
   125	
   126	# 5. Download failure -> falls through to the pre-existing cargo-install
   127	# fallback chain untouched: neither tar nor unzip invoked, cargo install
   128	# callisto-cli invoked, step still exits 0. Proves the new dispatch (which
   129	# now runs unconditionally before the if/elif chain) has no side effect on
   130	# that fallback.
   131	out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 1); code=$?
   132	if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
   133	  || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]] \
   134	  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]] \
   135	  || [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli"* ]]; then
   136	  echo "FAIL test_download_failure_falls_back_to_cargo_install: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   137	else
   138	  echo "PASS test_download_failure_falls_back_to_cargo_install"
   139	fi
   140	
   141	# 6. Verification success extracts only the binary in every mode but skip
   142	# (skip never calls gh); gh runs against the pinned repo and signer, before extraction.
   143	for mode in require fallback ""; do
   144	  out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0 ok "$mode"); code=$?
   145	  if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
   146	    || [[ "$out" != *"gh attestation verify "*"--repo orin-dx/callisto --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml"* ]] \
   147	    || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "*" callisto" ]] \
   148	    || [[ "${out%%tar -xzf*}" != *"gh attestation verify"* ]] \
   149	    || [[ "$out" == *"cargo install"* ]]; then
   150	    echo "FAIL test_verification_success_extracts_only_binary_${mode:-default}: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   151	  else
   152	    echo "PASS test_verification_success_extracts_only_binary_${mode:-default}"
   153	  fi
   154	done
   155	
   156	# 7. require + verification failure or missing gh aborts; asset never extracted or kept.
   157	for gh in fail missing; do
   158	  out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0 "$gh" require); code=$?
   159	  if [[ $code -eq 0 ]] || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"cargo install"* ]] \
   160	    || [[ "$out" == *"ASSET_PRESENT"* ]] || [[ "$out" != *"::error::"* ]]; then
   161	    echo "FAIL test_require_$([[ $gh == fail ]] && echo verification_failure || echo gh_missing)_aborts: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   162	  else
   163	    echo "PASS test_require_$([[ $gh == fail ]] && echo verification_failure || echo gh_missing)_aborts"
   164	  fi
   165	done
   166	
   167	# 8. fallback (explicit and default) + failure or missing gh: warn, delete the asset,
   168	# take crates.io, never extract.
   169	for gh in fail missing; do
   170	  for mode in fallback ""; do
   171	    out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0 "$gh" "$mode"); code=$?
   172	    name="test_fallback_$([[ $gh == fail ]] && echo verification_failure || echo gh_missing)_uses_crates_io_${mode:-default}"
   173	    if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]] \
   174	      || [[ "$out" == *"ASSET_PRESENT"* ]] || [[ "$out" != *"::warning::"* ]] \
   175	      || [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"cargo install --locked --git"* ]]; then
   176	      echo "FAIL $name: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   177	    else
   178	      echo "PASS $name"
   179	    fi
   180	  done
   181	done
   182	
   183	# 9. fallback keeps an explicit version pin and never uses the unpinned git install.
   184	out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0 fail fallback "callisto@0.5.0"); code=$?
   185	if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]] \
   186	  || [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli --version 0.5.0 "* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"--git"* ]]; then
   187	  echo "FAIL test_fallback_keeps_explicit_version_pin: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   188	else
   189	  echo "PASS test_fallback_keeps_explicit_version_pin"
   190	fi
   191	
   192	# 10. skip extracts without calling gh, with a warning.
   193	for gh in fail missing ok; do
   194	  out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0 "$gh" skip); code=$?
   195	  if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"gh attestation"* ]] \
   196	    || [[ "$out" != *"::warning::"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"cargo install"* ]]; then
   197	    echo "FAIL test_skip_extracts_without_gh_$gh: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   198	  else
   199	    echo "PASS test_skip_extracts_without_gh_$gh"
   200	  fi
   201	done
   202	
   203	# 11. Invalid value fails immediately, listing the valid values, with no download.
   204	out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0 ok bogus); code=$?
   205	if [[ $code -eq 0 ]] || [[ "$out" != *"valid values: require, fallback, skip"* ]] \
   206	  || [[ "$out" == *"curl"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]]; then
   207	  echo "FAIL test_invalid_verification_fails: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
   208	else
   209	  echo "PASS test_invalid_verification_fails"
   210	fi
   211	
   212	# 12. The action's declared input default is fallback.
   213	if grep -A12 '^  verification:' "$ACTION_YML" | grep -q "default: 'fallback'"; then
   214	  echo "PASS test_default_verification_is_fallback"
   215	else
   216	  echo "FAIL test_default_verification_is_fallback"; fail=1
   217	fi
   218	
   219	exit $fail
